_readme: RYB Comms bus configuration. CMake reads it at configure time and generates a config header
for the module being built; see include/ryb/README.md. Edit, then rebuild with
`cmake --build build`: CMake notices the change and re-reads this file.
Every board must build from the same version of this file, because they all have to agree on it.
Names under modules are the directories under modules/.
pins maps header pin names to io_switch numbers, which are also GPIO bit numbers (32..63 are
GPIO channel 2). The table is libpynq's pinmap.h for the TU/e io0.2.0 overlay: ARx is
Arduino digital pin x, RBPIx is pin x of the Raspberry Pi header.
_todo: Placeholders until the team records each decision in the protocol guideline:
modules.*.tx / rx: which header pin, and so which backbone conductor, each hop uses.
line.bit_period_us: shared by every board; the guideline leaves bit timing open.
line.drive: the guideline's open_drain needs a pull-up on each lane. Measured on a PYNQ-Z2
with the TU/e io0.2.0 overlay, a released Arduino pin took 6-9 ms to read high again, so
open_drain fails without an external pull-up (about 10 kOhm to 3.3 V). Until one is fitted,
push_pull is the default; CMake refuses two modules transmitting on the same pin in that mode.
The chain is one way, heartbeat -> sound -> decision -> motor; the motor only receives.
lcd.mosi: the module's DIN was reported on header pin 34, which is ground on a Pi header;
RBPI33 next to it is assumed. Confirm on the board.

_about: RYB_Displ3 (Waveshare 1.54in, ST7789, 240x240) seated on the Raspberry Pi header.
For an LCD on the Arduino header, as libpynq wires it by default: bl AR10, rst AR11,
dc AR12, cs AR13, sclk AR_SCL, mosi AR_SDA.
